change: Receive ordinary I420 socket bytes into an AVBufferPool allocation; transfer its AVBufferRef into an AVFrame instead of copying into a second allocation.

layout_policy.direct: Even frame dimensions and width divisible by 64: packed Y/U/V strides and plane starts are all 32-byte aligned. Includes 1920 and 320.
layout_policy.other_widths: Retain av_frame_get_buffer alignment and the original row copy path.
layout_policy.padding: Each pooled buffer has AV_INPUT_BUFFER_PADDING_SIZE extra bytes; zero this trailing margin before direct ownership transfer.

lifetime_policy: A no-frame PULL retains the private receive reference for reuse.
A delivered direct frame takes the receive reference; the next receive obtains a distinct free buffer.
Consumer references prevent a buffer from returning to the pool.
Flush does not overwrite or release consumer-owned frames.
stop_hardware releases the pending receive reference and calls av_buffer_pool_uninit; the upstream pool API defers final freeing until outstanding frame references are released.

direct_320: AVFrame pixel pointer equals the stub receive destination.
Two concurrently held frames have distinct backing memory and retain distinct contents.
After releasing frame two and flushing, its buffer is reused for frame three.
Frames one and three remain readable after decoder/pool shutdown.
unaligned_318: All Y/U/V strides are at least width and remain 32-byte aligned.
Held-frame contents survive flush and decoder shutdown.
validation.regression: Previous backpressure/EOS/timestamp/fatal checks plus all eight 45-frame H264/HEVC fallback sequences still match native pixel MD5, PTS, best_effort_timestamp and duration.

performance_review.removed_for_1080p: One 3,110,400-byte client-to-AVFrame CPU copy per delivered frame and repeated full-frame backing allocation once pooled buffers are reusable.
performance_review.remaining: WC-to-broker I420 copy; broker-to-kernel and kernel-to-client socket copies; any Firefox image/upload copy.
performance_review.transport: AF_UNIX SOCK_STREAM has no TCP Nagle or delayed-ACK timer. Separate headers add calls/wakeups; they do not imply a TCP-style fixed delay.
recommended_timing: frame payload receive duration and syscall count
broker backend pull versus socket send
wall clock versus thread CPU time and minor-fault deltas

limits: This record proves software buffer ownership and fallback behavior, not live performance or real hardware decode.
No broker restart, kernel change or new private DMA allocation is required by this library change.
AVBufferPool ordinary-RAM high-water use follows the number of frames retained by the consumer; it is not the private DMA heap.
Remaining WC-copy and transport costs require actual timing before claiming steady 60 Hz.
